channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Politico Europe] US central bank hikes interest rates and signals more to come, defying Trump
item.description: Central bankers are increasingly worried that inflation — worsened by soaring oil prices and an AI investment boom — is not on a path back to their 2% target.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump oil ally Harold Hamm to invest in Venezuela
item.description: Move by Continental Resources marks latest foray by a western oil producer into the country after US military seized president Nicolás Maduro

item.title: [Financial Times] Fed raises rates for first time since 2023 in unanimous decision
item.description: Central bank chair Kevin Warsh defies calls from Donald Trump to lower borrowing costs

item.title: [EU Observer] After the poison of Saxony-Anhalt, Berlin election could be the antidote
item.description: We hear a lot about extremism in Germany, after the breakthrough of the AfD earlier this month. Yet a far-left government may be about to take power in Berlin on Sunday, and is attracting almost no attention. Why is that?

item.title: [DW] UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
item.description: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU blindsided by von der Leyen’s Canada ‘associate member’ pitch
item.description: The Commission president unveiled the idea without consulting EU capitals — and Ottawa quickly tamped down expectations.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Hugging Face CEO: Advanced AI models require new transparency mandates
item.description: “I think there’s a lot to do around how to create better disclosures,” Clem Delangue said.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Von der Leyen fleshes out Carney’s vision to paint Europe as leader of world’s middle powers
item.description: European Commission president says she wants to “build global coalitions for our resilience and democracies.”

item.title: [Politico Europe] New EU security proposals risk fresh turf war with NATO
item.description: Proposals to give the EU crisis decision-making powers and hold emergency talks threaten to overlap with NATO's mission.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Anthropic policy chief says winning AI race key for safety
item.description: Sarah Heck underscored the need for new rules governing existential risk but said the U.S. must stay in the lead on AI.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Germany to send fighter jets to Latvia during election amid drone threat
item.description: Latvia's election is set for Oct. 3 and Riga has asked Germany for backup.

item.title: [DW] Can Canada and the EU build a deeper partnership?
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

item.title: [Politico Europe] Macron / von der Leyen : la course pour interdire les réseaux sociaux aux mineurs
item.description: C’est l’une des annonces majeures du « discours sur l’état de l’union » d’Ursula von der Leyen : la commission européenne va déposer une législation pour interdire les réseaux sociaux aux moins de 13 ans. Que propose-t-elle ? Pourquoi cette annonce intervient-elle aujourd’hui ? Pourquoi Emmanuel Macron s’active, malgré tout, pour imposer une loi allant […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Macron invites EU leaders to Pope Leo speech
item.description: The pontiff is expected to talk about Europe, peace and unity during an address in Metz.

item.title: [Financial Times] Bach choir is a rare symbol of unity in a swing state
item.description: In small-city Pennsylvania, music brings people together from across the political divide

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen’s ‘European values,’ paid for by private equity, powered by Claude
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen talks about European sovereignty and keeping Europe’s fate in European hands, but the model she presented for achieving that sovereignty relies heavily on non-European technology and global capital.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Von der Leyen’s call for talks on pausing AI can’t quell extinction risk fears
item.description: The EU chief used her annual State of the European Union address to confront rising panic about AI. What she said showed the limits on her power.

item.title: [DW] Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
item.description: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

item.title: [EU Observer] Belgian minister under fire for denying evacuation to 13 Gazan scholarship students
item.description: Belgium's minister for migration was accused of being "the shame of this government" during a heated debate on Wednesday on the fate of 13 Gazans who won scholarships to Belgian universities but have been denied transport so that they can take up their places.

item.title: [EU Observer] Turkey’s anti-LGBTI+ crackdown draws meek EU criticism
item.description: Turkey has arrested dozens of LGBTI+ activists in nationwide raids, drawing meek criticism from EU officials and calls for Europe-wide solidarity protests on Friday.

item.title: [DW] British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
item.description: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

item.title: [Financial Times] AI must not outrun safety controls, DeepMind co-founder warns
item.description: Shane Legg speaks to FT as new DeepMind Institute launches to explore implications of artificial general intelligence, amid growing calls for industry slowdown

item.title: [EU Observer] We lied to ourselves again, Russians write, as Ukrainians reportedly advance beyond the Zherebets river (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,665)
item.description: Ukrainians brace for another winter of blackouts, but are still overwhelmingly continuing resistance.

item.title: [EU Observer] Former Kosovo leader is war criminal rules EU-backed court, tearing open old Western Balkans wounds
item.description: Hashim Thaçi was convicted for "torture against 303 individuals and murder against 96 individuals", prompting angry protests by Kosovo nationalists in The Hague and Pristina.

item.title: [EU Observer] Did Europe’s ‘summer of truth’ push climate up von der Leyen’s agenda? Yes, but there were some shocking omissions
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen highlighted the devastating impacts of climate change during her State of the Union address, including hectares of land burned, crops lost and additional heatwave-related deaths.

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen set to cave in to Greek asylum-busting demands
item.description: The Greeks suspended asylum in 2020. They did it again last year. The EU commission endorsed both. Greece last month asked for new EU rules to suspend asylum and the commission appears to have complied.

item.title: [EU Observer] Canada’s Carney gets the red carpet treatment and EU ‘associate member’ offer
item.description: EU commission president Ursula von der Leyen offered unprecedented 'associate member' status of the bloc to Canada on Wednesday. But what could this mean in practice?

item.title: [Financial Times] Chinese oil prices hit record highs after attacks on Saudi pipeline
item.description: Beijing has cushioned global impact of Iran war by drawing down stocks but is now ‘coming off its crash diet’

item.title: [DW] Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
item.description: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

item.title: [Financial Times] AI bosses’ safety push sparks rift inside OpenAI and Anthropic
item.description: Staff at the Silicon Valley companies are grappling with how to turn AI slowdown rhetoric into reality

item.title: [EU Observer] Putin and Netanyhau will be laughing at EU after von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech
item.description: EU Commission president Ursula von der Leyen's answer to spiralling Russian aggression was one new strategy document and two new sets of meetings. Her answer to Israel's killing spree was to call it "unacceptable".

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Russia has never stopped thinking like an empire — here’s how it shapes and may break the Kremlin
item.description: When other empires stopped expanding, Russia refused to stop. "Perhaps Russia was too successful for too long," argues political geographer Michael Romancov. He explained that over five centuries of land grabs worked for so long it became part of Russia's "genetic make-up".

item.title: [DW] Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
item.description: A Hague tribunal ruled that Hashim Thaci, a former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), is responsible for war crimes carried out during the war of independence with Serbia.

item.title: [ECFR] An outsider within: The paradox of the Europe-Turkey relationship
item.description: Turkey is neither drifting away from the West nor is it coming home. It has become an embedded outsider: a middle power that has learned to build strategic autonomy from inside the Western system rather than by leaving it.

item.title: [Financial Times] Von der Leyen backs Canada’s ‘associate membership’ bid
item.description: European Commission president says EU and Canada ‘see the world with the same eyes’

item.title: [Financial Times] EU to restrict social media and chatbots for children under 15
item.description: Ursula von der Leyen describes AI as ‘second tipping point of our time’ after climate change

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: What should Europeans expect from Ursula von der Leyen on climate?
item.description: With summer droughts, fires and rising food insecurity fresh in mind, von der Leyen is expected to weigh only modest moves like a new Water Act and climate-risk plan.

item.title: [Financial Times] World’s best-performing sovereign wealth fund expects equities pullback
item.description: New Zealand’s superannuation fund grows 14% despite being underweight on US tech stocks

item.title: [Financial Times] Nuclear fusion’s moment of truth
item.description: Start-ups are attracting record investments. Some scientists think their timelines are far too optimistic

item.title: [Financial Times] Iran’s hidden leader stirs unease at home
item.description: Mojtaba Khamenei’s absence from public view has been a source of bafflement and suspicion

item.title: [ECFR] A future with Chinese characteristics
item.description: The world is undergoing a historical and cultural rupture. Just as Hollywood and other American exports once gave the rest of the world a glimpse of modern life and the future that awaited them, China is now doing the same for African, Latin American and even American young people

item.title: [ECFR] Friends without benefits: Why the EU should offer Canada more than casual defence ties
item.description: Trump is pushing Canada—a quiet military powerhouse—away from America. The EU should seize the chance and fold it into its own defence

item.title: [DW] Turkey's rights groups, EU call out LGBTQ+ crackdown
item.description: Several raids and arrests of LGBTQ+ persons in Turkey have triggered sharp criticism from numerous Turkish organizations — and also from Brussels.

item.title: [EU Observer] The EU’s 15 year self-declared war against migrant smugglers is a deadly joke
item.description: Magnus Brunner, the EU migration commissioner, makes an impassioned plea to tackle migrant smugglers. The EU has been saying the same thing for the past 15 years, yet profits remain high and people continue to die.

item.title: [DW] Why do authoritarian regimes target the LGBTQ+ community?
item.description: A recent crackdown on the LGBTQ+ community in Turkey is symptomatic of a wider rights regression, according to experts. It's worse under authoritarian regimes, but why is it such a popular policy for these states?

item.title: [EU Observer] Von der Leyen’s State of the Union likely to tiptoe around China ahead of trade showdown
item.description: The EU's competitiveness problems and its trade dispute with China have not gone away, but Ursula von der Leyen won't pile on the criticism of Beijing at Wednesday's State of the Union address, as trade talks enter the crunch stage.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU sanctions needed against Russian bot and troll factories, MEPs say
item.description: The parliament supports the European Democracy Shield proposal and calls for sanctions to fight Russian disinformation campaigns.

item.title: [ECFR] Indian summer: The BRICS summit and warming New Delhi-Beijing relations
item.description: Xi Jinping’s attendance at the BRICS summit in New Delhi underlines the recent normalisation in Sino-Indian relations. This should encourage the EU to speed up its efforts to deepen ties with India

item.title: [ECFR] Life of the party: Democrats and the search for a post-Trump future
item.description: The race for US midterms reveals a rapidly changing Democratic party. Europeans must understand and engage its three camps well before the party could take power

item.title: [DW] Netherlands: Suspected sabotage disrupts train services
item.description: A major outage has hit parts of the Dutch railway system after objects were found placed across lines, authorities say. The company responsible for rail infrastructure says it suspects deliberate wrongdoing.

item.title: [DW] Europe launches two climate observation satellites
item.description: The European Space Agency has put two satellites into orbit to take a closer look at the impact of climate change. One of them will focus particularly on plant life.

item.title: [ECFR] Future nostalgia: Europe’s unfinished song
item.description: ECFR’s new research reveals Europeans are suffering from an imagination gap. Many people want to see Europe strong and flourishing—but fewer can picture a credible route from today’s disruptions to that destination

item.title: [ECFR] Beyond Saxony-Anhalt: What Merz’s crisis means for Europe
item.description: The far-right AfD’s win in a small German state calls for dynamism in Berlin and hedging in Brussels

item.title: [ECFR] Emergency Room: The AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Jana Puglierin, senior policy fellow and head of ECFR’s Berlin office, to discuss the Alternative for Germany (AfD)’s election win in Saxony-Anhalt—and what it means for Germany and Europe

item.title: [ECFR] Britons back ban on trade with Israeli settlements by more than two to one
item.description: New polling published by ECFR shows that Britons across the political divide favour banning trade with illegal Israeli settlements

item.title: [ECFR] Booted, then suited: Veterans and the making of Putin’s new proto-elite
item.description: The Kremlin is promoting Ukraine war veterans--cultivating a proto-elite who could reinforce Russia’s militarised course.

item.title: [DW] Russians on the Goethe-Institut: 'Hostage to politics'
item.description: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia has affected their lives.

item.title: [DW] EU seeks Arctic strategy amid growing power rivalry
item.description: Russia's aggression, Trump's threats against Greenland and the race for critical raw materials are pushing the Arctic to the top of Europe's agenda.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine, Russia set for new round of US-mediated talks
item.description: New trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US could begin in October, according to Kyiv and Moscow. Few expect a breakthrough, but Ukraine is seeking a partial de-escalation to help it get through the winter.

item.title: [DW] Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
item.description: Donald Trump, under fire for record US diesel prices, claims Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking energy targets. Russia said nothing; Ukraine said "we expect specifics from our partners" on any such move.

item.title: [DW] EU leaders urge unity after Russian strike on train
item.description: Russia's drone attack on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border has triggered EU calls to up support for Kyiv. Allies of Ukraine should show they "are not scared," said the bloc's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas.

item.title: [ECFR] Against war, drought and hunger: A global coalition to prevent a food crisis
item.description: Three features of today’s unordered world are converging to create a devastating food crisis. Russia’s war in Ukraine is disrupting agricultural exports from both countries. The enduring blockage of the Strait of Hormuz is restricting fertiliser shipments. And this year’s El Niño (a sporadic warming of the Pacific Ocean generating widespread knock-on effects elsewhere) could […]

item.title: [ECFR] Remembering Emma Bonino
item.description: ECFR founding member and co-chair emerita Emma Bonino has died at the age of 78. A towering figure in European foreign policy, she was an inspiration to millions across the continent. She left a deep mark on European and Italian politics, and on ECFR

item.title: [ECFR] The EU’s unfinished business in the Western Balkans
item.description: Montenegro and Albania are moving closer to EU membership. But Brussels should not forget its responsibility towards the Western Balkans as a whole

item.title: [ECFR] The geopolitics of global hunger
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Cary Fowler and Jim O’Brien to discuss the factors behind the escalating risk of a major food crisis—and Europe’s role in preventing catastrophe

item.title: [ECFR] Ukraine: The battle beyond war
item.description: Jessica Hendrick welcomes Roman Petrov and Svitlana Zalishchuk to discuss Ukraine’s simultaneous fight for survival on the frontlines and battle for democracy at home
